verses.text: This saying is trustworthy: if someone wants to serve as an overseer, they desire a good work.
So an overseer must be above reproach, faithful to one wife, clear-minded, self-controlled, respectable, welcoming to guests, and able to teach.
They must not be a drunkard or violent, but gentle, not argumentative or greedy for money.
They must manage their own household well and have children who respect them.
If someone doesn't know how to manage their own household, how can they care for God's church?
They must not be a recent convert, or they may become conceited and fall into the same judgment as the devil.
They must also have a good reputation with outsiders, so they won't fall into disgrace or the devil's trap.
In the same way, church servants must be dignified, sincere, not drinking too much wine, and not chasing dishonest gain.
They must hold on to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
Let them first be tested; then, if nothing is found against them, let them serve.
In the same way, women must be dignified, not slanderers, clear-minded, and faithful in everything.
Church servants must be faithful to one wife and manage their children and households well.
Those who serve well earn a good standing and great confidence in the faith they have in Christ Jesus.
I'm writing these things to you, though I hope to come to you soon.
If I'm delayed, you'll know how people should conduct themselves in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

Without question, the mystery of godliness is great: He was revealed in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and taken up in glory.
